title: defenseclaw-gateway enterprise linux tetragon verify [--ready-for MODE] --json
description: Whether this host is ready for a Tetragon mode: the mode its config asks for, or the one --ready-for names. Read from the installed config, the sensor helper's published state, Tetragon's info file, /sys/kernel/security/lsm and the unit states; the command changes nothing and never connects to Tetragon. ok and exit_code 0 mean no check failed; warn and info checks never fail it. Additive changes keep schema_version 1.

mode.description: The mode this host runs as its config renders it (empty when the command stopped before it read the config).

kernel_policy.description: The kernel-control digest this build ships: the value enforce_ack approves, the same on every host of the build.

fix.description: Copy-paste lines: commands as root runs them, or YAML for the admin config.

users.description: With ready_for enforce: each enrolled user's burn-in on this host.

state.description: The sensor helper's state of the user: enforcing, burn_in, monitor or inactive.

reason.description: The sensor helper's reason for the state. kernel_pid_anchor_monitor_only and kernel_binary_anchor_scope_limited mark a user that finished burn-in but stays in monitor without a deny anchor of its own.

ready.description: Enforce would deny for the user now: the burn-in finished (or the user is enforcing), one of its connectors is in action mode, and the sensor helper does not keep it in monitor for want of a deny anchor.

reset.description: A would-block hit restarted the burn-in window.

measuring.description: The window is younger than 24h, so there is no ETA yet.

monitor_only.description: No connector of the user is in action mode: enforce never denies for it (guardrail_observe), whatever the burn-in says.

eta_hours.description: Calendar hours until ready at the user's rate of agent use so far.

phase.description: The one word a fleet summary counts the user by. held: finished burn-in or limited, and not denied (a deny-anchor limit, a pause, an operator's change); ready is held while the host runs enforce.

path.description: The most frequent path, home-relative (~/...) for the user's own files.
